ELMALILI:67:20-22/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r9.claim: The disbeliever crawls face-down like an animal, with eyes fixed on low things and no regard for others, and will crawl similarly in Hell.
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r9.anchor: yüzün koyu sürüne sürüne hayvan gibi

ELMALILI:67:20-22/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r10.claim: The upright monotheist believer, walking straight on the clear road with faith and knowledge, is more rightly guided; people should consider which way to follow.
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r10.anchor: iman ve irfan ile doğru bir cadde üzerinde eğrilmeden dümdüz Hakk’a giden muvahhid, müstakīm mü’minler mi daha iyi, daha hidâyetkâr olur?

ELMALILI:67:20-22/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r11.claim: Human life is meant to proceed uprightly toward God, not to crawl like a low animal while seeking food only on earth.
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r11.anchor: İnsan olan bir düşünmelidir. Şüphesiz ki insanlık

ELMALILI:67:20-22/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r12.claim: People should first believe in the Creator's oneness and laws, follow His proofs, open broad material and spiritual paths, and walk directly toward Him.
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r12.anchor: Hâlık’ın birliğine ve ahkâmına iman ederek ve O’nun gösterdiği delâili tâkip eyleyerek maddeten ve mânen doğru ve geniş

ELMALILI:67:20-22/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r13.claim: The straight path is the religion of tawhid, and walking it straight means living with moral rectitude within the bounds of ethics and sacred law.
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r13.anchor: İşte bu sırât-ı müstakīm Hak dini olan tevhid yoludur. Ve onda düz gitmek de istikāmetle ahlâk ve şeriat dairesinde yürümektir.

ELMALILI:67:20-22/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r14.claim: The first practical consequence is removing harmful obstacles and filth from roads, making them broad and clean, and walking them justly without encroaching on others.
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r14.anchor: bunun muktezâsından birincisi إِمَاطَةُ الأَْذَى عَنِ الط َّرِيقِ yani yoldan ezâ verecek, mâni‘aları pislikleri kaldırarak

ELMALILI:67:20-22/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r15.claim: He links this ethic of creating broad, usable paths to God's making the earth a carpet for people to follow its spacious routes.
ELMALILI:67:20-22/r15.anchor: Allah teâlâ Sûre-i Nûh’ta geleceği üzere Nûh 71/19-20][^13]] وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًۭا لِّتَسْلُكُوا۟ مِنْهَا سُبُلًۭا فِجَاجًۭا

ASAD-NOTES:67:21#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:67:21#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:67:21#n19/r1.claim: Walking prone symbolizes spiritual obtuseness: a person sees only immediate worldly concerns and has no sense of the direction of the path, like an earthworm.
ASAD-NOTES:67:21#n19/r1.anchor: seeing only what is immediately beneath his feet, and utterly unaware of the direction into which his path is taking him

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:67:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:67:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:67:22/r1.claim: The verse symbolically contrasts an ungrateful unbeliever, spiritually blind and following Satan on false paths, with a believer on the right path, asking who will reach the goal more safely and without straying.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:67:22/r1.anchor: Şeytanlara uyarak, mânevî körlük içinde bâtıl yollarda giden inkârcı nankör ile hak yolda yürüyen mümin temsilî olarak karşılaştırılmakta

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p402/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p402/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p402/r10.claim: People enslaved to desire never reach the true goal; only those who stay on the right path do so.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p402/r10.anchor: Those who lead their lives while remaining slaves to their desires will never reach the real goal. Only those who remain on the right path will reach this goal.

QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#1/r1.claim: This canonical ishmām gives ṣād a slight zāy sound, preserving a trace of the word's non-Arabic origin as an intermediate pronunciation between sīn and ṣād.
QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: ṣād with ishmām (slight admixture of zāy sound) — preserves a phonological trace of the word's non-Arabic origin

QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#2/r1.speaker: Qālūn ʿan Nāfiʿ
QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#2/r1.claim: The canonical sīn reading is closer to the etymological source Latin strāta and is accepted by Qālūn ʿan Nāfiʿ; it makes no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:67:22:12#2/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with sīn instead of ṣād — closer to etymological source (Latin strāta); accepted by Qālūn ʿan Nāfiʿ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r1.claim: Qatadah says the one walking face-down is a disobedient unbeliever who will be resurrected on his face.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أفمن يمشي مكبا ﴾ قال هو الكافر عمل بمعصية الله فيحشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r2.claim: When asked how people could walk on their faces, the Prophet says the One who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r2.anchor: فذكر أنه قيل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف يمشون على وجوههم قال إن الذي أمشاهم على أقدامهم قادر على أن يمشيهم على وجوههم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r3.claim: Qatadah says the one walking upright on a straight path is a believer who obeyed God and will be resurrected in obedience.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p305#3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أم من يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم ﴾ قال المؤمن عمل بطاعة الله فحشره الله على طاعته

BURSEVI:v10p72/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p72/r1.claim: The contrast is a parable illustrating the condition of the polytheist and the monotheist.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r1.anchor: مثل ضرب للمشرك والموحد توضيحا لحالهما

BURSEVI:v10p72/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p72/r2.claim: The interrogative hamza precedes the conjunction in form because it must lead; in meaning the order is reversed, as a question with هل would show.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r2.anchor: والفاء لترتيب ذلك على ما ظهر من سوء حالهم وتقديم الهمزة عليها صورة

BURSEVI:v10p72/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p72/r3.claim: مكبا means fallen face-down; grammatically it is a circumstantial accusative describing the walker, who repeatedly stumbles and falls because the path is rough and his strength impaired.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r3.anchor: والمكب الساقط على وجهه وحقيقته صار ذاكب ودخل في الكب

BURSEVI:v10p72/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r4.speaker: صاحب المناسبات
BURSEVI:v10p72/r4.claim: He explains that God does not call the first person's course a path because it is undeserving of that name.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r4.anchor: قال في المناسبات لم يسم سبحانه لمشيانه طريقا لأنه لا يستحق ذلك

BURSEVI:v10p72/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p72/r5.claim: The word أهدى allows for someone to find an easy route by chance rather than insight, so the comparison asks who is truly better guided.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r5.anchor: ولما كان ربما صادق السهل لا عن بصيرة بل عن اتفاق قال أهدى

BURSEVI:v10p72/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r6.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v10p72/r6.claim: One interpretation takes the face-down walker as a metaphor for a blind person who cannot find the way, unlike a sighted person.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r6.anchor: وقيل المكب كناية عن الأعمى لأنه لا يهتدي إلى الطريق فيتعسف

BURSEVI:v10p72/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p72/r7.claim: The Persian couplet contrasts clear-sighted certainty on the path of religion with a blindfolded person wandering by guesswork.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r7.anchor: با آنكه دوشم بسته بي دست كسى هركوشه همي رود بظن وتخمين

BURSEVI:v10p72/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r8.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v10p72/r8.claim: The unbeliever obeys sin in this life and is gathered face-down toward Hell, while the believer follows God's command and is gathered on his feet toward Paradise.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة هو الكافر أكب على معاصي الله في الدنيا فحشره الله على وجهه

BURSEVI:v10p72/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r9.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p72/r9.claim: When asked how people could walk on their faces, the Prophet replied that the One who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r9.anchor: قيل للنبي عليه السلام ، وكيف يمشون على وجوههم قال إن الذي أمشاهم

BURSEVI:v10p72/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p72/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p72/r10.claim: The verse alludes to God revealing on Judgment Day the good or evil a person kept hidden in this life.
BURSEVI:v10p72/r10.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى يظهر للإنسان يوم القيامة ما أبطن اليوم خيرا أو شرا

QASHANI:67:22-23/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:67:22-23/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:67:22-23/r1.claim: The face-down walker turns toward the lower realm, loves sensual pleasures, and is drawn to natural things; the upright walker follows the fully straight path of unity.
QASHANI:67:22-23/r1.anchor: متنكسا بالتوجه إلى الجهة السفلية ومحبته للملاذ الحسية وانجذابه إلى الأمور الطبيعية

QASHANI:67:22-23/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:67:22-23/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:67:22-23/r2.claim: The straight path of unity is so completely upright that its full nature and measure cannot be attained or estimated.
QASHANI:67:22-23/r2.anchor: على صراط التوحيد الموصوف بالاستقامة التامة التي لا يبلغ كنهها ولا يقدر قدرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r1.claim: Qatada says the verse describes the Resurrection: unbelievers walk on their faces while believers walk upright; on this view the image is literal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r1.anchor: قال قتادة نزلت مخبرة عن حال القيامة، وأن الكفار يمشون فيها على وجوههم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r2.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r2.claim: In a report answering how an unbeliever can walk on his face, the Prophet says the One who made him walk on his feet in this world can make him walk on his face in the next; the author says Qatada's reading is literal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r2.anchor: إن الذي أمشاه في الدنيا على رجليه قادر أن يمشيه في الآخرة على وجهه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r3.claim: They take the walking as a general metaphor for the disbeliever and believer in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو مجاز، ضرب مثلا للكافر والمؤمن في الدنيا. فقيل: عام، وهو قول ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r4.claim: A separate report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the comparison concerns Abu Jahl and the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: نزلت في أبي جهل والرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r5.claim: Another view places the verse about Abu Jahl and Hamza; the unbeliever's confused doctrine is like a blind person stumbling, while the believer follows a clear, easy path with a settled heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r5.anchor: وقيل: في أبي جهل وحمزة، والمعنى أن الكافر في اضطرابه وتعسفه في عقيدته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r6.claim: Mukibban is a circumstantial accusative from akabba, which is intransitive; kabb is transitive, and its hamza marks entering a state or becoming so.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r6.anchor: ومكبا: حال من أكب، وهو لا يتعدى، وكب متعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari claims no form on the afʿala pattern is a direct responsive form; the author criticizes this claim as ignorance of Sibawayh's text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r7.anchor: ولا شيء من بناء افعل مطوعا، ولا يتقن نحو هذا إلا حملة كتاب سيبويه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r8.claim: The author attacks al-Zamakhshari for repeatedly boasting of Sibawayh while missing passages, and notes that Abu al-Hajjaj Yusuf ibn Maʿzuz wrote a book listing his errors and ignorance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r8.anchor: وكم من نص في كتاب سيبويه عمي بصره وبصيرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r9.claim: Ahdā appears to be a comparative of guidance; the question is rhetorical, since every listener would answer that the upright walker on a straight path is better guided.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r9.anchor: وهذا الاستفهام لا تراد حقيقته، بل المراد منه أن كل سامع يجيب بأن الماشي سويا على صراط مستقيم أهدى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r10.claim: Qalīlan is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; mā is extra, and tashkurūn may begin a new clause or be an anticipated circumstantial clause, meaning they give little thanks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r10.anchor: وانتصب قليلا على أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف، وما زائدة، وتشكرون مستأنف أو حال مقدرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the unbelievers give some thanks, but it is little and useless; alternatively, “little” may idiomatically mean no thanks at all.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p228/r11.anchor: ظاهر أنهم يشكرون قليلا، وما عسى أن يكون للكافرين شكر، وهو قليل غير نافع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r1.claim: The image compares the polytheist with the monotheist, clarifying their worldly conditions and the truth of their two creeds; the fronted interrogative has its semantic order reversed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r1.anchor: مثل ضرب للمشرك والموحد توضيحا لحاليهما في الدنيا وتحقيقا لشأن مذهبيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r2.claim: Grammatically, the first man is a relative-subject with ‘walking’ as its clause, ‘stumbling’ as its circumstance, and ‘more guided’ as predicate; the second is conjoined, so no omitted predicate is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r2.anchor: ومن موصولة مبتدأ ويمشي صلته ومكبا حال من الضمير المستتر فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r3.claim: The fallen man repeatedly stumbles because his route is uneven, while the upright man follows a level, straight path; the disbeliever’s way is not even called a path, and ‘more guided’ is comparative.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى أفمن يمشي وهو يعثر في كل ساعة ويخر على وجهه في كل خطوة لتوعر طريقه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r4.speaker: ابن سيده، الجوهري، ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r4.claim: Ibn Sīda, al-Jawharī, Ibn al-Ḥājib, and others explain akabba as ‘became prone to falling,’ with the hamza of transformation, not as the regular reflexive of kabb.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم التحقيق أن الهمزة فيه للصيرورة فمعنى أكب صار ذا كب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī records both kabbahu and akabbahu as transitive forms, a usage supported by the lexicon and removing the apparent irregularity.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r5.anchor: وحكى ابن الأعرابي كبه الله تعالى وأكبه بالتعدية وفي القاموس ما هو نص فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r6.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about Abū Jahl and Ḥamza; another report from him gives the comparison its general scope, also reported from Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r6.anchor: والآية على ما روي عن ابن عباس نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة وحمزة رضي الله تعالى عنه والمراد العموم كما روي عن ابن عباس أيضا ومجاهد والضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r7.claim: Qatāda reads the comparison as the disbelievers’ and believers’ conditions in the afterlife: disbelievers walk on their faces and believers upright.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة نزلت مخبرة عن حال الكافر والمؤمن في الآخرة فالكفار يمشون فيها على وجوههم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r8.claim: When asked how a disbeliever could walk on his face, the Prophet replied that the One who made him walk on his feet in this world can make him walk on his face in the next; on this reading it is not a parable.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r8.anchor: وروي أنه قيل للنبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كيف يمشي الكافر على وجهه فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام أن الذي أمشاه في الدنيا على رجليه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r9.claim: Another reading takes the stumbling man as blind and the upright walker as sighted, by metonymy or metaphor; this can still exemplify the broader comparison.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p19#2/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمكب الأعمى وبالسوي البصير وذلك إما من باب الكناية أو من باب المجاز المرسل

QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r13.claim: People were specially given hearing, sight, and hearts yet fail to thank God for these great blessings.
QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r13.anchor: وخصكم بالسمع والبصر والأفئدة ، وأنتم لا تشكرون عظيم نعمه

QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r17.claim: All these verses function as arguments against the deniers, and none of them had an answer.
QUSHAYRI:v3p338/r17.anchor: وهذه الآيات جميعها على وجه الاحتجاج عليهم . . . ولم يكن لواحد عن ذلك جواب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r8.claim: The person walking face-down is the disbeliever, recklessly astray and blind in heart and eyes, while the believer walks upright, sees the road, and follows a straight path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r8.anchor: {أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه} راكبا رأسه في الضلالة والجهالة أعمى القلب والعين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r9.claim: Qatāda says the disbeliever is made to walk on his face at Resurrection because he was bent over sins in worldly life, while the believer walks upright that day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p179#2/r9.anchor:
قال قتادة: أكب على 170/ب المعاصي في الدنيا فحشره الله على وجهه
يوم القيامة

BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r3.claim: The verb akabba is an unusual form; it means becoming one who has fallen, like aqshaʿa means becoming cloudless, rather than being the passive of kabba.
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r3.anchor: يقال كببته فأكب وهو من الغرائب كقشع الله السحاب فأقشع

BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r4.claim: The true passive forms are ankabba and inqašaʿa; mukib describes someone who repeatedly stumbles and falls face-first on a rough, uneven road.
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r4.anchor: بل المطاوع لهما أنكب وانقشع، ومعنى { مكبا } أنه يعثر كل ساعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r5.claim: The upright walker moves safely without stumbling on a straight, even path; the contrast depicts the disbeliever and monotheist as travelers on two religions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r5.anchor: { أمن يمشى سويا } قائما سالما من العثار. { على صرط مستقيم } مستوي الأجزاء والجهة

BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r6.claim: The rough route is left implicit to suggest that the polytheist’s way scarcely deserves to be called a path.
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r6.anchor: ولعل الاكتفاء بما في الكب من الدلالة على حال المسلك للإشعار بأن ما عليه المشرك لا يستأهل أن يسمى طريقا

BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r7.claim: Alternatively, the face-down person is blind and stumbles, while the upright walker can see.
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمكب الأعمى فإنه يتعسف فينكب وبالسوي البصير

BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r8.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r8.claim: Another interpretation says the first person is resurrected face-first toward the Fire, while the upright one is resurrected on his feet toward Paradise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:67:21-22/r8.anchor: وقيل من { يمشى مكبا } هو الذي يحشر على وجهه إلى النار ومن { يمشى سويا }

BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r7.claim: The question compares a monotheist and an idolater as travelers following two different ways of life.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r7.anchor: ممثلا للموحد والشمرك بسالكين ولدينيهما بمسلكين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r8.claim: The face-down walker represents an irrational, crooked course, stumbling because he cannot see and desire and ignorance pull him from the way.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r8.anchor: وهو كناية عن السير على رسم مجهول وأثر معوج معلول , على غيره عادة العقلاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r9.claim: Repeated hardship does not deter this walker from the cause of his stumbling, so his route is not even dignified as a path.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r9.anchor: فهو بحيث لا يكون تكرار المشاق عليه زاجرا له عن السبب الموقع له فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r10.claim: Someone may encounter level ground by coincidence rather than discernment; that accident does not make him better guided.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p81/r10.anchor: ربما صادف السهل لا عن بصيرة بل اتفاقا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r1.claim: The upright walker raises his head, avoids stumbling, and sees ahead and to either side.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r1.anchor: قائما رافعا رأسه ناصبا وجه سالما من العثار لأنه لانتصابه يبصر ما أمامه وما عن يمينه وما عن شماله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r2.claim: His road is broad, prepared, easy, straight, and fully level.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r2.anchor: طريق موطأ واسع مسلوك سهل قويم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r3.claim: This walker represents someone who accepts God as Lord and Islam as religion, following the original nature untainted by desire, anger, or self-interest.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r3.anchor: هذا مثل من رضي بالله ربا وبالإسلام دينا فإنه يتبع الفطرة الأولى السليمة عن شهوة أو غضب أو شائبة حظ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r4.claim: The unbeliever sees neither surrounding signs nor what he hears, consumed by desire and ignorance as he travels toward God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r4.anchor: لا يرى ما حوله ولا يشعر بما أحاط به , ولا ينظر في الآيات ولا يعتبر بالمسموعات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r5.claim: The unbeliever's concealed condition in this life will become manifest at resurrection, when he is gathered face-down to Hell as recompense.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r5.anchor: فيحشر على وجهه إلى النار جزاء لرضاه بحالته هذه في هذه الدار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r6.claim: The verse uses the rhetorical figure of omission by pairing: the first description implies its opposite in the second, and the second implies the first's opposite, highlighting the criminal's worst feature and the Muslim's best.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r6.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الكب أولا دليلا على ضده ثانيا , والمستقيم ثانيا دليلا على المعوج أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r7.claim: The Arabs prized knowing physical routes and thanking benefactors, but the deniers err in the more honored spiritual route by opposing the Messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r7.anchor: فنفي عنهم الأول بقيام الأدلة على خطئهم الفاحش في كل ما خالفوا فيه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من طريقهم المعنوي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r8.claim: The command to speak recalls God's protection, benefits, powers, and intellect so they may return to Him and walk uprightly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p82/r8.anchor: مذكرا لهم بما دفع عنهم الملك من المفاسدات وجمع لهم من المصلحات والقوى والعقل ليرجعوا إليه

TUSTARI:67:22/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:67:22/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:67:22/r1.claim: The person bent toward the self's desire by innate disposition lacks guidance from his Lord and is the misguided alternative in the comparison.
TUSTARI:67:22/r1.anchor: مطرقا إلى هوى نفسه بجبلة طبعه بغير هدى من ربه

TUSTARI:67:22/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:67:22/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:67:22/r2.claim: The upright walker follows Islam's laws and takes the prophets as models.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3363#6/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3363#6/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3363#6/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas contrasts one who walks face-down, meaning in error, with one who walks upright, meaning guided.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3363#6/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما افمن يمشي مكبا قال : في الضلال امن يمشي سويا قال : مهتديا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r1.claim: Commentators agree the image compares disbelievers and believers, or two men, but they do not explain which group each image represents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r1.anchor: وذلك مما اتفق عليه المفسرون على اختلاف مناحيهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r2.claim: Without assigning the first image to idolaters and the second to believers, the warning loses force and readers may think each side is the other's bad example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r2.anchor: ولكن لم يعرج أحد منهم على بيان كيف يتعين التمثيل الأول للكافرين والثاني للمؤمنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r3.claim: He rejects a supposedly evenhanded reading like 34:24: this passage belongs to argument and proof, not mutual concession or softening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r3.anchor: ويتوهم أن الكلام ورد على طريقة الكلام المنصف نحو { وإنا أو إياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين } ( سبأ : 24 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r4.claim: He reads the two figures as the polytheist and monotheist, with religion represented as a road and the idolater moving along a crooked path.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r4.anchor: والذي انقدح لي : أن التمثيل جرى على تشبيه حال الكافر والمؤمن بحالة مشي إنسان مختلفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r5.claim: The crooked-path image portrays a confused traveler who studies tracks because he cannot trust the twisting route to his destination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r5.anchor: كما يقتضيه قوله : { على صراط مستقيم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r6.claim: The polytheist divides worship among many tribal gods, unsure which is more powerful or more favorably disposed to his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r6.anchor: فالمشرك يتوجه بعبادته إلى آلهة كثيرة لا يدري لعل بعضها أقوى من بعض وأعطف على بعض القبائل من بعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r7.claim: He cites Thaqīf worshipping al-Lāt and Aws and Khazraj worshipping Manāt as familiar examples of tribal division among idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r7.anchor: فقد كانت ثقيف يعبدون اللات ، وكان الأوس والخزرج يعبدون مناة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r8.claim: The appeal to Joseph's question about scattered lords reinforces the contrast between many gods and the One, All-Dominant God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r8.anchor: أأرباب متفرقون خير أم الله الواحد القهار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r9.claim: He explains the image through the contrast between Islam's single straight path and the divided ways of idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r9.anchor: فقابل في الآية الأولى الصراط المستقيم المشبه به الإسلام بالسبل المتفرقة المشبه بها تعداد الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r10.claim: The next cited verse likewise presents Islam as a path followed with insight and distinguishes its caller from the polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p44/r10.anchor: وقوله : { قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعن وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين } ( يوسف : 108 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r1.claim: The verse contains three representational metaphors, including the polytheist's uncertain search among gods for something beneficial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r1.anchor: فالآية تشتمل على ثلاث استعارات تمثيلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r2.claim: The first image is a traveler on a road without a clear highway, following winding side paths and looking for other people's tracks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r2.anchor: بحال السائر قاصدا أرضا معينة ليست لها طريق جادة فهو يتتبع بنيات الطريق الملتوية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r3.claim: Within the larger metaphor, face-down walking depicts the traveler's extreme closeness to the ground while searching for traces.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r3.anchor: وفي ضمن هذه التمثيلية تمثيلية أخرى مبنية عليها بقوله : { مكبا على وجهه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r4.claim: The upright walker represents a believer confident in one Lord, His help, and the truth, like a traveler on a clear main road.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r4.anchor: وقوله : { أمن يمشي سويا } تشبيه لحال الذي آمن برب واحد الواثق بنصر ربه وتأييده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r5.claim: The first road's crookedness is left unstated because the second road's being straight makes the contrast clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r5.anchor: وقد حصل في الآية إيجاز حذف إذ استغني عن وصف الطريق بالالتواء في التمثيل الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r6.claim: The opening fa makes the comparison follow from all the preceding signs, and the question seeks acknowledgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r6.anchor: والفاء التي في صدر الجملة للتفريع على جميع ما تقدم من الدلائل والعبر من أول السورة إلى هنا ، والاستفهام تقريري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r7.claim: Mukibb is the active participle of akabba; its hamza marks entering a state, like a cloud entering a clearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r7.anchor: والمكب : اسم فاعل من أكب ، إذا صار ذا كب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r8.claim: Ahda means knowing the way, but its superlative form is not comparative here because the face-down walker has no guidance at all.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r8.anchor: و { أهدى } مشتق من الهدى ، وهو معرفة الطريق وهو اسم تفضيل مسلوب المفاضلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r9.claim: Many leading scholars take the noncomparative superlative in Joseph 12:33 similarly; such usage can carry mockery or light irony.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p45/r9.anchor: فهو من باب قوله تعالى : { قال رب السجن أحب إلي مما يدعونني إليه } ( يوسف : 33 ) في قول كثير من الأيمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r1.claim: Sawiyy means fully upright and is an active-participle form; he cites the phrase “a straight path.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r1.anchor: والسوي : الشديد الاستواء فعيل بمعنى فاعل قال تعالى : { أهدك صراطا سويا } ( مريم : 43 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r2.claim: The second am coordinates with the interrogative hamza, and both instances of man are relative pronouns referring to the two groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r2.anchor: و ( أم ) في قوله : { أمن يمشي سويا } حرف عطف وهي ( أم ) المعادلة لهمزة الاستفهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r3.claim: A reported alternative identifies the first person as Abū Jahl and the second as the Prophet, Abū Bakr, or Ḥamza.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p46/r3.anchor: وقيل : أريد شخص معين أريد بالأولى أبو جهل ، وبالثانية النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أو أبو بكر أو حمزة رضي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r1.claim: The image is of a blind person who cannot see right, left, or what is before him.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r1.anchor: لا يبصر يمينا ولا شمالا ولا ما بين يديه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r2.claim: He notes the usage أكب فلان على وجهه with the added alif, versus كبه الله لوجهه without it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p475#6/r2.anchor: يقال: أكب فلان على وجهه (بالألف) ، وكبه الله لوجهه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r3.speaker: رواة الأسباب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r3.claim: A group of occasion-of-revelation transmitters say the parable was about Abu Jahl and Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r3.anchor: واختلف أهل التأويل في سبب قوله: أفمن يمشي مكبا الآية، فقال جماعة من رواة الأسباب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الكلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r4.claim: They and others say the parable contrasts Abu Jahl with Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن الكلبي وغيره: نزلت مثلا لأبي جهل بن هشام ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r5.claim: They also give a general reading: the parable represents believers and disbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا ومجاهد والضحاك: نزلت مثالا للمؤمنين والكافرين على العموم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r6.claim: He says the verse describes Resurrection, when disbelievers walk on their faces and believers upright.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: نزلت مخبرة عن حال القيامة، وإن الكفار يمشون فيها على وجوههم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r7.claim: Asked how a disbeliever can walk on his face, the Prophet answers that the One who made him walk on his legs in this world can make him walk on his face in the next.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r7.anchor: «إن الذي أمشاه في الدنيا على رجليه قادر على أن يمشيه في الآخرة على وجهه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r8.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r8.claim: He says the first three readings make the walking figurative, while Qatada's Resurrection reading makes it literal; the disbelievers then undergo the two contrasting states.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r8.anchor: ففي الأقوال الثلاثة الأول المشي مجاز يتخيل، وفي القول الرابع هو حقيقة يقع يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r9.claim: Akabba means a man turned his face toward the earth, while kabba means he turned someone face-down; the pattern reverses the usual transitivity of afʿala and faʿala, as in qashaʿat the wind / aqshaʿat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r9.anchor: أكب الرجل، إذا رد وجهه إلى الأرض، وكبه: غبره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r10.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r10.claim: The Prophet says that what throws people into Hell is the harvest of their tongues, illustrating the transitive form kabba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r10.anchor: «وهل يكب الناس في النار إلا حصائد ألسنتهم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r11.claim: Ahdā is the comparative form of hudā, guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r11.anchor: وأهدى في هذه الآية أفعل من الهدى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r12.speaker: طلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p342/r12.claim: He reads “or the one who walks” with an ungeminated mīm.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the face-down walker sees neither right nor left nor ahead; the idiom describes the blind person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي لا يبصر يمينا ولا شمالا ولا من بين يديه يقال أكب فلان على وجهه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r2.claim: The exegetes take the comparison as a likeness of believer and unbeliever; the upright walker sees the road.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون هذا مثل للمؤمن والكافر والسوي المعتدل أي الذي يبصر الطريق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r3.claim: Qatada locates the comparison in the afterlife: God gathers the unbeliever face down and the believer walking upright.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p323#3/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة هذا في الآخرة يحشر الله الكافر مكبا على وجهه والمؤمن يمشي سويا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r3.claim: The verse compares disbeliever and believer: the disbeliever wanders face-down, unable to choose a way, while the believer stands upright on a clear, straight path.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r3.anchor: فالكافر مثله فيما هو فيه كمثل من يمشي مكبا على وجهه، أي: يمشي منحنيا لا مستويا على وجهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r4.claim: This contrast applies in both lives: the believer is resurrected upright toward Paradise, while the disbeliever is dragged on his face to Hell, as in the gathering passage of 37:22–26.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r4.anchor: فالمؤمن يحشر يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم، مفض به إلى الجنة الفيحاء، وأما الكافر فإنه يحشر يمشي على وجهه إلى نار جهنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r5.claim: Anas reports that when people asked how they would be gathered on their faces, the Prophet answered that the One who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p181/r5.anchor: عن نفيع قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول: قيل: يا رسول الله، كيف يحشر الناس على وجوههم؟ فقال: "أليس الذي أمشاهم على أرجلهم قادرا

JISHUMI:v10p7012/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7012/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7012/r10.claim: Ikbāb is falling face-first; its verb is unusual because a form normally made causative is here intransitive, while kabb can be transitive.
JISHUMI:v10p7012/r10.anchor: والإكباب: الإلقاء على الوجه، أكب يكب إكبابا فهو مكب فيما لا يتعدى

JISHUMI:v10p7012/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7012/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7012/r11.claim: The verb pattern is contrasted with the usual transitive-to-intransitive pair, as in ‘I drove the clouds apart and they dispersed.’
JISHUMI:v10p7012/r11.anchor: وهذا على ضده، يقال: كببته على وجهه فأكب، ونظيره: قشعت الريح السحاب فانقشعت.

JISHUMI:v10p7013/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r13.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take the face-down walker as a parable for the unbeliever and the upright walker as a parable for the believer.
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r13.anchor: قيل: ضرب مثلا للمؤمن والكافر، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v10p7013/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r14.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r14.claim: Qatāda reads the image literally: the unbeliever will be resurrected walking on his face on Judgment Day.
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو على الحقيقة، فإن الكافر يحشر يوم القيامة يمشي على وجهه، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7013/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r15.claim: Other explanations make the face-down person fallen and unable to see or walk the road, or blindly immersed in error and unable to distinguish truth from falsehood.
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r15.anchor: قيل: ساقطا على وجهه، فلا يرى الطريق، ولا يقدر على المشي، وقيل: أفمن يمشي راكبا رأسه في الضلالة كالأعمى

JISHUMI:v10p7013/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r16.claim: The upright walker on a clear, straight road is more guided because he knows the way, unlike one without knowledge.
JISHUMI:v10p7013/r16.anchor: وهذا تقدير أن من يمشي سويا يعلم الطريق هو أهدى ممن لا علم له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r1.claim: He rejects treating akabba as a regular intransitive passive of kabba: this is an anomalous analysis, and no afʿala pattern is a regular passive; the regular intransitive is inkabba.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r1.anchor: يقال : كببته فأكب ، من الغرائب والشواذ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r2.claim: Rather, akabba belongs with forms such as infaḍḍa and alʾama: it means entering a state and becoming bent over; qashʿa/aqshaʿ works similarly, while the passive forms are inkabba and inqashaʿa.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r2.anchor: ومعناه : دخل في الكب ، وصار ذا كب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r3.claim: The bent-over person walks awkwardly over uneven familiar ground and repeatedly falls on his face, unlike someone walking upright without falling; alternatively, he deviates from a straight path.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r3.anchor: يمشي معتسفا في مكان معتاد غير مستو فيه انخفاض وارتفاع ، فيعثر كل ساعة فيخر على وجهه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation contrasts a blind person groping off course and repeatedly falling with a sound-sighted person walking straight on a guided path; the comparison represents believer and unbeliever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الأعمى الذي لا يهتدي إلى الطريق فيعتسف ، فلا يزال ينكب على وجهه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says the unbeliever bent over God's disobedience and will therefore be gathered face-down on Judgment Day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة : الكافر أكب على معاصي الله تعالى فحشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r6.speaker: الكلبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the bent-over person as Abū Jahl and the upright walker as the Messenger; another report names Ḥamza as the upright person.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p586#2/r6.anchor: وعن الكلبي : عني به أبو جهل بن هشام . وبالسوي : رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وقيل : حمزة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r1.claim: The verse is a parable about guidance and misguidance: the face-down walker cannot see ahead or to either side, unlike an upright walker who looks around.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r1.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى للهدى والضلالة , ومعناه ليس من يمشي مكبا على وجهه ولا ينظر أمامه ولا يمينه ولا شماله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the face-down walker is the disbeliever stumbling in disbelief and the upright walker the believer guided by faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r2.anchor: ومعناه : أمن يمشي في الضلالة أهدى أم من يمشي مهتديا , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r3.claim: Ikrima identifies the face-down walker as Abu Jahl and the upright walker as Ammar ibn Yasir.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : أن المكب على وجهه أبو جهل بن هشام , ومن يمشي سويا عمار بن ياسر , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r4.claim: One gloss of the straight path is a clear road whose traveler does not go astray; this describes the parable.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r4.anchor: أن الطريق الواضح الذي لا يضل سالكه , فيكون نعتا للمثل المضروب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says the straight path is the upright truth, whose consequence is uprightness and the end of guidance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p56#2/r5.anchor: هو الحق المستقيم , قاله مجاهد , فيكون جزاء العاقبة الاستقامة وخاتمة الهداية

MUJAHID:v2p686/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p686/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p686/r1.claim: Mujahid contrasts walking face-down in misguidance with walking upright on the straight path of truth.
MUJAHID:v2p686/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ مكبا على وجهه ﴾ يعني في الضلالة ﴿ أم من يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم ﴾ يعني على الحق المستقيم

MUQATIL:67:18-22/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:67:18-22/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:67:18-22/r4.claim: Abu Jahl, the disbeliever, walks astray, fallen on his face and blind in heart; Muhammad walks upright as a believer on Islam's straight path with a pure heart.
MUQATIL:67:18-22/r4.anchor: يعني الكافر يمشي ضالا في الكفر أعمى القلب، يعني أبا جهل بن هشام

NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.claim: One person walks face-down, falling and stumbling at every moment and wandering aimlessly; the other walks upright, safely, on a straight road.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه ﴾ أي ساقطا على وجهه يعثر كل ساعة ويمشي معتسفا وخير من ﴿ أهدى ﴾ أرشد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.claim: The comparison asks which person is better guided; the straight path is an even road.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ على صراط مستقيم ﴾ على طريق مستو

NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.claim: The predicate after man is omitted because the word ahda already indicates it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r3.anchor: وخبر من محذوف لدلالة اهدى عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.speaker: الكلبي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the one face-down as Abu Jahl and the upright walker as the Prophet.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p266#3/r4.anchor: وعن الكلبي عني بالمكبأبو جهل وبالسوي النبي عليه السلام

NAHHAS:v4p471/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p471/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p471/r7.claim: من is a nominative subject with أهدى as predicate; أم من يمشي سويا is coordinated with it.
NAHHAS:v4p471/r7.anchor: من في موضع رفع بالابتداء أهدى خبره ( أم من يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم ) عطف عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r1.claim: The verse offers an image contrasting the believer and unbeliever.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r1.anchor: ضرب الله مثلا للمؤمن والكافر { مكبا } أي منكسا رأسه لا ينظر أمامه ولا يمينه ولا شماله

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r2.claim: The face-down walker cannot see ahead or to either side and risks stumbling, unlike an upright walker who looks around and follows the way.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r2.anchor: فهو لا يأمن من العثور والانكباب على وجهه. كمن يمشي سويا معتدلا ناظرا ما بين يديه وعن يمينه وعن شماله.

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r3.claim: The image can describe worldly life, or a blind person unable to find the road and repeatedly falling, unlike a sound, sighted person guided along it.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا في الدنيا ويجوز أن يريد به الأعمى الذي لا يهتدي إلى الطريق فيعتسف فلا يزال ينكب على وجهه.

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r4.claim: The unbeliever bowed over God's disobedience in this life will be raised on his face on Judgment Day.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو الكافر أكب على معاصي الله في الدنيا فحشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه.

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r5.claim: They identify the face-down walker as Abū Jahl and the upright walker as the Messenger of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والكلبي: عنى بالذي يمشي مكبا على وجهه أبا جهل، وبالذي يمشي سويا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r6.claim: One reported identification makes Abū Bakr the upright walker.

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r7.claim: Another reported identification makes Ḥamza the upright walker.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r7.anchor: وقيل أبو بكر. وقيل حمزة. وقيل عمار ابن ياسر قاله عكرمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r8.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r8.claim: Ikrima identifies ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir as the upright walker.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r8.anchor: وقيل حمزة. وقيل عمار ابن ياسر قاله عكرمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r9.claim: A general reading contrasts an unbeliever unsure whether he is right or wrong with a Muslim who sees the way and walks upright on Islam's straight path; the author also explains the intransitive and transitive forms of akabba.
QURTUBI-FULL:67:22/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو عام في الكافر والمؤمن أي أن الكافر لا يدري أعلى حق هو أم على باطل. أي أهذا الكافر أهدى أو المسلم الذي يمشي سويا معتدلا يبصر للطريق وهو { على صراط مستقيم } وهو الإسلام. ويقال: أكب الرجل على وجهه فيما لا يتعدى بالألف. فإذا تعدى قيل: كبه الله لوجهه بغير ألف.

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī calls أكب a passive counterpart of كب, as in كببته فأكب, and compares it with قشعت الريح السحاب فأقشع.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي : أكب مطاوع كبه ، يقال : كببته فأكب

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r2.claim: The Kashshāf author objects that أكب means entering a state; the true passive counterparts of كب and قشع are انكب and انقشع.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r2.anchor: بل قولك : أكب معناه دخل في الكب وصار ذا كب

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r3.claim: One image is a person crossing uneven ground, stumbling and repeatedly falling face-first, unlike someone walking steadily without falling.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r3.anchor: في مكان غير مستو بل فيه ارتفاع وانخفاض فيعثر كل ساعة ويخر على وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r4.claim: Another image contrasts a confused wanderer moving this way and that in ignorance with someone who knows the destination with certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r4.anchor: المتعسف الذي يمشي هكذا وهكذا على الجهالة والحيرة

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r5.claim: A third image is a blind person groping and falling versus a sighted, healthy person following a known road.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r5.anchor: الأعمى الذي لا يهتدي إلى الطريق فيتعسف ولا يزال ينكب على وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r6.claim: Qatāda reads the image as the afterlife: the sinner who bent over God's disobedience is raised face-down, while the believer on clear religion is raised on a straight path.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة : الكافر أكب على معاصي الله فحشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r7.claim: Others take the image as a worldly contrast between believer and disbeliever, and between learned and ignorant people.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r7.anchor: بل هذا حكاية حال المؤمن والكافر والعالم والجاهل في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r8.claim: Some say the description is general to all believers and disbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r8.anchor: هذا عام في حق جميع المؤمنين والكفار

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r9.claim: Muqātil says the specific pair is Abū Jahl and the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r9.anchor: فقال مقاتل : المراد أبو جهل والنبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r10.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, reporting from Ibn ʿAbbās, identifies the pair as Abū Jahl and Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس : المراد أبو جهل وحمزة بن عبد المطلب

RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r11.speaker: عكرمة
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r11.claim: ʿIkrima identifies the pair as Abū Jahl and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir.
RAZI-FULL:v30p64#2/r11.anchor: وقال عكرمة هو أبو جهل وعمار بن ياسر

STUDYQURAN:67:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r1.claim: The face-down walker is a metaphor for disbelievers who ignore the path around them and fail to consider their real condition, absorbed in petty and immediate desires.
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r1.anchor: One who walks with his face stooped down is seen as a metaphor for disbelievers, who do not look at the path ahead, to the right, or to the left in this life (Q, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:67:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r2.claim: The image is also read as referring to disbelievers gathered face-down for Hell in 25:34.
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r2.anchor: It is also seen as a reference to the state of disbelievers in the Hereafter; as 25:34 says

STUDYQURAN:67:22/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r3.claim: Believers walk upright, seeing the way and avoiding afflictions that could lead them astray.
STUDYQURAN:67:22/r3.anchor: In contrast, believers are said to walk upright, so that they see and are not beset by afflictions that would cause them to go astray.

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r1.claim: He compares a person who stumbles face-down without seeing around him with one who walks upright on a straight path, asking which is better guided.

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r2.claim: He explains the straight path as one with no crookedness and gives a grammatical account of the form akabba: an intransitive verb takes an added alif, unlike the transitive form.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r2.anchor: على طريق لا اعوجاج فيه؛ وقيل {مكبا} [سورة: الملك، آية رقم: 22] لأنه فعل غير واقع، وإذا لم يكن واقعا أدخلوا فيه الألف

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line uses mukibban as evidence for the intransitive form, with the fallen camel digging at its sides.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r3.anchor: قول الأعشى: [البحر الطويل] مكبا على روقيه يحفر عرقها

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the face-down walker as one in error and the upright walker as guided.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم} [الملك: 22] يقول: من يمشي في الضلالة أهدى

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says the face-down walker is in error, while the upright walker follows a true straight path.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {مكبا على وجهه} [الملك: 22] قال: في الضلالة {أمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم} [الملك: 22] قال: حق مستقيم

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the face-down walker with an unbeliever and the upright walker with a believer, as a parable of the two.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r6.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه} [الملك: 22] يعني الكافر {أهدى أمن يمشي سويا} [الملك: 22] المؤمن، ضرب الله مثلا لهما

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r7.claim: Another view says the unbeliever will be resurrected face-down on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى بذلك أن الكافر يحشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r8.claim: Qatada says the unbeliever committed disobedience in this world and will be raised on his face; he reports the Prophet's answer that the one who made people walk on feet can raise them face-down.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى} [الملك: 22] «هو الكافر أكب على معاصي الله في الدنيا، حشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه»

TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r9.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r9.claim: The Prophet says the one who made the unbeliever walk on his feet is able to resurrect him on his face.
TAB-FULL:v23p132#2/r9.anchor: فقيل: يا نبي الله، كيف يحشر الكافر على وجهه؟ قال: «إن الذي أمشاه على رجليه قادر أن يحشره يوم القيامة على وجهه»

TAB-FULL:v23p134/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r1.claim: Qatada says the unbeliever who acts disobediently will be raised on his face.
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه} [الملك: 22] قال: «هو الكافر يعمل بمعصية الله، فيحشره الله يوم القيامة على وجهه»

TAB-FULL:v23p134/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r2.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r2.claim: The Prophet says the one who made people walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r2.anchor: قال معمر: قيل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: كيف يمشون على وجوههم؟ قال: «إن الذي أمشاهم على أقدامهم قادر على أن يمشيهم على وجوههم»

TAB-FULL:v23p134/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r3.claim: Qatada says the upright walker is a believer who acted in obedience and will be resurrected upon his obedience.
TAB-FULL:v23p134/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم} [الملك: 22] قال: المؤمن عمل بطاعة الله، فيحشره الله على طاعته

SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r1.claim: مكبا is a circumstantial accusative modifying the subject of يمشي.
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r1.anchor: قوله: { مكبا }: حال من فاعل " يمشي ".

SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls أكب a rare intransitive Form IV, not a regular reflexive; it means entering the state of كب or becoming bent over, like forms meaning entering a state.
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " هو من الغرائب والشواذ ونحوه: قشعت الريح السحاب فأقشع، ولا شيء من بناء أفعل مطاوعا،

SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r3.claim: The Shaykh says أكب is intransitive while كب is transitive; the hamza marks entering a state or becoming it, and the actual reflexive of كب is انكب.
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r3.anchor:
قال الشيخ ": " ومكبا " حال من " أكب " وهو لا يتعدى، وكب متعد قال تعالى:
فكبت وجوههم في النار
[النمل: 90] والهمزة للدخول في الشيء أو للصيرورة

SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r4.claim: The author accuses the Shaykh of copying al-Zamakhshari's explanation and then attacking him discourteously; he doubts the cited critic's accuracy and quotes a poet on criticizing sound words through poor understanding.
SAMIN-DURR:67:22/r4.anchor: وانظر إلى هذا الرجل: كيف أخذ كلامه الذي أسلفته عنه، طرز به عبارته حرفا بحرف، ثم أخذ ينحي عليه بإساءة الأدب،

SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r1.claim: أمن يمشي is the counterpart to أفمن يمشي مكبا.
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: { أمن يمشي } هو المعادل ل { أفمن يمشي مكبا }.

SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa takes أهدى as the predicate of the first من يمشي and supplies an omitted predicate for the second.
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: و " أهدى " خبر " من يمشي " ، وخبر " من " الثانية محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r3.claim: The author says no ellipsis is needed: in “Is Zayd standing, or Amr?” the second noun is coordinated with the first, and أم asks which of two things, so one predicate suffices.
SAMIN-DURR:67:22#2/r3.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى ذلك، لأن قوله: " أزيد قائم أم عمرو " لا يحتاج فيه من حيث الصناعة إلى حذف الخبر،

TABATABAI:67:19-21/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r9.claim: Akabba means to cast something down on its face.
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r9.anchor: إكباب الشيء على وجهه إسقاطه عليه

TABATABAI:67:19-21/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r10.speaker: الزمخشري في الكشاف
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains akabba as entering into al-kabb and becoming face-down.
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r10.anchor: وقال في الكشاف معنى أكب دخل في الكب وصار ذا كب

TABATABAI:67:19-21/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r11.claim: The rhetorical question denies that the two states are equal, after the obstinate have been distanced from the honor of direct address.
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r11.anchor: استفهام إنكاري عن استواء الحالين تعريضا لهم بعد ضرب حجاب الغيبة عليهم

TABATABAI:67:19-21/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r12.claim: A face-down traveler cannot see rises, dips, hazards, or the destination as an upright walker on a straight path can.
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r12.anchor: فليس هذا السائر كمن يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم فيرى موضع قدمه وما يواجهه من الطريق

TABATABAI:67:19-21/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r13.claim: The disbelievers knowingly defy truth, turning away from what they must know and do instead of following life's path with insight and safety from ruin.
TABATABAI:67:19-21/r13.anchor: هؤلاء الكفار سائرون سبيل الحياة وهم يعاندون الحق على علم به فيغمضون عن معرفة ما عليهم أن يعرفوه

TABATABAI:67:22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:67:22/r1.claim: The verse is a general parable of the ignorant, obstinate unbeliever and the believer who seeks truth with insight.
TABATABAI:67:22/r1.anchor: مثل عام يمثل حال الكافر الجاهل اللجوج المتمادي على جهله والمؤمن المستبصر الباحث عن الحق

TABATABAI:67:22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:67:22/r2.claim: A report in al-Kafi describes four hearts: one combining faith and hypocrisy, an inverted heart, a sealed heart, and a bright heart.
TABATABAI:67:22/r2.anchor: قال القلب أربعة قلب فيه نفاق وإيمان، وقلب منكوس، وقلب مطبوع، وقلب أزهر

TABATABAI:67:22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:67:22/r3.claim: The bright heart is like a lamp and belongs to the believer, who gives thanks when granted and remains patient when tested; the sealed heart is the hypocrite's and the inverted heart the polytheist's.
TABATABAI:67:22/r3.anchor: قال فيه كهيئة السراج. فأما المطبوع فقلب المنافق، وأما الأزهر فقلب المؤمن إن أعطاه شكر وإن ابتلاه صبر

TABATABAI:67:22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:67:22/r4.claim: The report identifies the inverted heart with the polytheist and recites this verse about the one walking face-down.
TABATABAI:67:22/r4.anchor: وأما المنكوس فقلب المشرك ثم قرأ هذه الآية { أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه أهدى أم من يمشي سويا على صراط مستقيم }

TABATABAI:67:22/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:67:22/r5.claim: The mixed faith-and-hypocrisy heart refers to people at al-Ta'if: dying in hypocrisy means ruin, while dying in faith means salvation.
TABATABAI:67:22/r5.anchor: فأما القلب الذي فيه إيمان ونفاق فقوم كانوا بالطائف فإن أدرك أحدهم أجله على نفاقه هلك

TABATABAI:67:22/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:67:22/r6.claim: The report's al-Ta'if means a demonic visitation that afflicts a person; those people perish if it is present at death and are saved if they die in faith.
TABATABAI:67:22/r6.anchor: المراد به الطائف الشيطاني الذي ربما يمس الإنسان قال تعالى إن الذين اتقوا إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان تذكروا

TABATABAI:67:22/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r7.speaker: ابن بابويه عن الفضيل عن سعد الخفاف عن أبي جعفر
TABATABAI:67:22/r7.claim: Al-Burhan transmits the same four-heart report, with a variant calling the bright heart luminous as well.
TABATABAI:67:22/r7.anchor: إلا أن فيه وقلب أزهر أنور

TABATABAI:67:22/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:67:22/r8.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:67:22/r8.claim: Some reports apply the verse to those who oppose Ali's authority and to his followers and allies; Tabataba'i classifies this as application, not the verse's direct interpretation.
TABATABAI:67:22/r8.anchor: هناك روايات تطبق قوله { أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه } الآية على من حاد عن ولاية علي عليه السلام

ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r3.claim: The believer follows a straight way, while the disbeliever in error resembles someone walking face-down.
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r3.anchor: أعلم الله - عز وجل - أن المؤمن سالك الطريقة المستقيمة، وأن الكافر في ضلالته بمنزلة الذي يمشي مكبا على وجهه.

ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r4.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r4.claim: An interpretation says the disbeliever will literally walk on his face in the afterlife.
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r4.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الكافر يمشي على وجهه في الآخرة.

ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r5.speaker: رسول الله
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r5.claim: Asked how people will walk on their faces, the Prophet replied that the One who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
ZAJJAJ:v5p200/r5.anchor: وسئل رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: كيف يمشون على وجوههم؟ فقال: الذي مشاهم على أرجلهم قادر على أن يمشيهم على وجوههم.

THALABI:v9p359/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p359/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p359/r14.claim: Walking face-down means headlong in error and ignorance, blind in heart and eyes and unable to see either side; it describes the unbeliever.
THALABI:v9p359/r14.anchor: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه راكبا رأسه في الضلالة والجهالة أعمى القلب والعين لا يبصر يمينا ولا شمالا، وهو الكافر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r7.claim: The person who walks face-down represents disbelievers, wandering in error and blind of heart; the upright person sees the road and walks Islam’s straight path.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r7.anchor: فضرب المكب على وجهه مثلا للكفار؛ لأنه أكب على وجهه في الغي والكفر يمشي ضالا أعمى القلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r8.claim: “Bending face-down” is the causative/reflexive form of casting someone down; it is also said of one wandering heedlessly in error.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r9.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي ومقاتل ومجاهد والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r9.claim: They identify the straight path as Islam and describe the believer as walking upright and seeing the way.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r9.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي، وقول مقاتل، ومجاهد، والضحاك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r10.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r10.claim: He depicts the disbeliever as following his own head into disbelief and misguidance like a beast.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r10.anchor: راكبا رأسه في الكفر والضلالة كما تركب البهيمة رأسها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r11.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r11.claim: The two figures are Abu Jahl and the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r11.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني أبا جهل والنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r12.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r12.claim: The two figures are Abu Jahl and Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r12.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد أبا جهل وحمزة بن عبد المطلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r13.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r13.claim: The two figures are Abu Jahl and Ammar ibn Yasir.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r13.anchor: وقال عكرمة (¬1): هو أبو جهل وعمار بن ياسر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r14.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r14.claim: He applies the image to the hereafter: the disbeliever is resurrected face-down, while the believer walks upright, as in 17:97.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p58/r14.anchor: هذا في الآخرة يحشر الله الكافر مكبا على وجهه يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r2.claim: The disbeliever is resurrected walking on his face; the believer walks upright along a straight path.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r2.anchor: أفمن يمشي مكبا على وجهه } أي: الكافر يحشر يوم القيامة وهو يمشي على وجهه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r3.claim: The wording uses a reflexive form: one is thrown face down, and he falls onto his face.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:67:21-22/r3.anchor: يقال: كببت فلانا على وجهه فأكب هو.

BURHAN:v3p131/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p131/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p131/r5.claim: Each half of the paired comparison omits what the other supplies; the comparative requires four elements, and the implicit answer is that the one walking upright on a straight path is more guided.
BURHAN:v3p131/r5.anchor: فإن فيه جملتين حذف نصف كل واحدة منهما اكتفاء بنصف الآخرى وأصل الكلام أفمن يمشي مكبا

BURHAN:v1p423/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p423/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p423/r1.claim: The script separates عن ما when the universal “what” contains real subcategories with different rulings, which عن applies to individually.
BURHAN:v1p423/r1.anchor: معنى ما عموم كلى تحته أنواع مفصلة فى الوجود غير متساوية فى حكم النهى عنها

BURHAN:v1p423/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p423/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p423/r5.claim: The أم من in 67:22 is joined because the two walkers belong to one type, walking on a straight path; أم من جعل الأرض قرارا is likewise joined because it has no subdivisions.
BURHAN:v1p423/r5.anchor: فهذا موصول لأنه من نوع واحد حيث يمشى على صراط مستقيم

BURHAN:v1p423/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p423/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p423/r7.claim: ممن is always joined: the conceptual distinction between من and ما does not divide into separate entities in existence.
BURHAN:v1p423/r7.anchor: وكذلك ممن موصول كله لأن من بفتح الميم جزئى بالنسبة إلى ما

DAMGHANI:v1p253/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r8.claim: Sawiyy can mean just or upright; the person walking evenly on a straight path is guided justly.
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r8.anchor: السوي العدل قوله تعالى في سورة طه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r5.claim: A fourth sense is rightly guided; the person walking uprightly on a straight path is glossed as guided.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السوي في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r1.claim: The root's Qur'anic use occurs only as this imperfect verb in seven verses; ameh denotes bewilderment, transgression, heedlessness, and blindness of insight, near to literal blindness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r1.anchor: وليس فى القرآن من المادة غير هذا الفعل المضارع فى الآيات السبع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r2.speaker: الخليل ويعقوب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r2.claim: Arabic calls a landmarkless area al-ard al-amha; the phrase for camels disappearing describes their vanishing when no one knows where they went.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r2.anchor: والأرض العمهاء فى العربية، التى لا أعلام فيها. وقالوا ذهبت إبلُه العُمَّهْى، حين لا يدرى أين ذهبت

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r3.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r3.claim: Ibn al-Athir compares spiritual bewilderment to physical blindness, saying it repeatedly occurs in hadith.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r3.anchor: والتفت "ابن الأثير " إلى صلة بين العمه والعمى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p581/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains ya'mahoon as running headlong without seeing, and compares it to the person walking face down rather than upright on a straight path.
